newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's PM acknowledges reform, economy concerns.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's PM acknowledges reform, economy concerns.

text.p: Vietnam's Prime Minister, Vo Van Kiet, has acknowledged concern among international donors about Vietnam's economic reform process, pledging commitment to addressing those worries.

Kiet, speaking in an interview with Reuters ahead of the weekend, said he was pleased by the results of a World Bank Consultative Group meeting in Hanoi earlier this month at which donors backed Vietnam's reforms with $2.4 billion in new aid.
"... the conference also made a couple of warnings. The three problems raised by the donors, I think, they are very correct, very correct. We very much appreciated that assessment... ," he said.
Donors told Vietnam at the two-day meeting to reduce its reliance on external capital, improve the investment environment and work to extend the benefits of growth from cities to rural areas.
The government was also urged to improve its administrative mechanisms and streamline aid management policies.
Kiet said Hanoi would do its best to tackle the issues and thereby reciprocate the goodwill shown by donors.
"I very much welcomed the results of the donation," he said. "It is an indication of continued support by the international community of donors for Vietnam."
Vietnam has enjoyed a position for several years as a darling of the internationl aid community.

World Bank officials said that despite the concerns expressed over Vietnam's economic management, donors had decided to push ahead with the new 1997 aid package in recognition of the efforts being made by Hanoi to transform its economy.
This month's meeting brought total pledges to $8.5 billion since 1993, when international financial instutions resumed lending to Hanoi.
